subject: Part4 error related to defaultGuiderOnset and possible solution

messages.author: 42e46cfeb9067366
messages.subject: Part4 error related to defaultGuiderOnset and possible solution
parts:
Dear colleagues,

When processing our actigraphy data using GGIR, we noticed that a number of raw data files (about 15 out of 155) generated an error message during Part 4:
"Error in if (is.na(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero”

After some investigation, we traced the error message back to function g.sib.det(). See below our processes and proposed solution:
  1. The printed error message occurred in line 297 in g.part4.R
    1. The issue is from the variable defaultGuiderOnset having a NULL value (which results in is.na(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE to have length 0).
    2. To find out why the variable defaultGuiderOnset is NULL, we noted that it takes its value from SPTE_start[j], as assigned on line 292.
    3. SPTE_start came from the meta.sleep.folder, which contains RData outputs generated by function g.part3().
      1. We compared the milestone 3 files from data files that ran successfully and files that failed and observed that in the data frame "sib.cla.sum," files that failed contained the value 0 in the night variable, while files that ran to completion had night indexes starting at 1.
  2. We looked at the g.part3.R file to find out where the values for the variable night were generated.
    1. The data frame "sib.cla.sum" is created by the function g.sib.sum() in line 118, and this function requires an input parameter "SLE."
    2. SLE was generated using the function g.sib.det() in line 82.
  3. From here, we looked at g.sib.det.R.
    1. The variable night is initialized in line 116 to contain the value of 0.
    2.  These values were later modified according to another variable, sptei, which was initialized as 0 in line 221.
    3. We believe the problem lies in lines 230 and 231, where nights containing data under 60 epochs were skipped, and the sptei was not updated in the next line (i.e., at this point, for these nights, sptei == 0).
    4. It follows that, for nights under 60 epochs, the variable night will have a value of 0.
  4. So, in g.part4.R, when the defaultGuiderOnset variable is set to SPTE_start[j], where “j” is the location index in the list nnights.list (line 265) and that a location index of 0 will result in NULL values, we know the following:
    1. min(sib.cla.sum$night) == 0, for these problematic files
    2. (lines 216-217) first_night = min(sib.cla.sum$night)
      last_night = max(sib.cla.sum$night)
    3. (line 219) nnightlist = first_night:last_night
    4. (line 226) nnights.list = nnightlist
  5. Since “j” will be of value 0 in the first iteration of the for-loop starting at line 265, we will see SPTE_start[j] == NULL, and consequently, defaultGuiderOnset == NULL.
In our specific cases, we can address this issue by running GGIR() separately for input data files that crashed due to this error by skipping their first night in part 4 (by adding the argument "excludefirst.part4 = TRUE" to GGIR()). However, for replicability purposes, it is not ideal that these input files will be run using a slightly different shell script than the rest of the inputs.

We wanted to share these with the rest of the GGIR community in case anyone else has run into a similar issue. If helpful, we would also like to propose a potential fix in the source code so that this won't be an issue for future projects:
  1. In file g.sib.det.R OR g.sib.sum.R, whichever is more convenient and appropriate, consider implementing a change such that the final output is free of rows in which night is equal to 0.
    • Sample code: df <- df %>% filter(night !=0), where df is the name of the output data frame ("metatmp" or "sib.cla.sum," depending on where the change is implemented).
    • The reason why we think this fix might work is because the nights with night = 0 are, by design and reason of too little data, to be skipped. Therefore, dropping those rows should not be a major cause of concern.
We hope some of you might find this information helpful -- thanks!

Best,
Grace

Dear Vincent 

I am also getting a similar error ("Error in if (is.na(defaultGuider)) { : argument is of length zero") with GGIR v3.1-2 and v3.1-5 when processing data files that were collected during the change of daylight savings. I was able to proceed with the analysis by skipping their first night in part 4 (by adding the argument "excludefirst.part4 = TRUE" to GGIR()) as suggested by Grace. Attached are the milestone data for a few data files to assist with the investigation. 

Thank you.

Best regards,
John.

On Monday, 22 July 2024 at 10:46 PM, Jiaxin “Grace” Chen <rusc...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear colleagues,

When processing our actigraphy data using GGIR, we noticed that a number of raw data files (about 15 out of 155) generated an error message during Part 4:
"Error in if (is.na(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE) { : argument is of length zero”

After some investigation, we traced the error message back to function g.sib.det(). See below our processes and proposed solution:
  1. The printed error message occurred in line 297 in g.part4.R
    1. The issue is from the variable defaultGuiderOnset having a NULL value (which results in is.na(defaultGuiderOnset) == TRUE to have length 0).
    2. To find out why the variable defaultGuiderOnset is NULL, we noted that it takes its value from SPTE_start[j], as assigned on line 292.
    3. SPTE_start came from the meta.sleep.folder, which contains RData outputs generated by function g.part3().
      1. We compared the milestone 3 files from data files that ran successfully and files that failed and observed that in the data frame "sib.cla.sum," files that failed contained the value 0 in the night variable, while files that ran to completion had night indexes starting at 1.
  2. We looked at the g.part3.R file to find out where the values for the variable night were generated.
    1. The data frame "sib.cla.sum" is created by the function g.sib.sum() in line 118, and this function requires an input parameter "SLE."
    2. SLE was generated using the function g.sib.det() in line 82.
  3. From here, we looked at g.sib.det.R.
    1. The variable night is initialized in line 116 to contain the value of 0.
    2. These values were later modified according to another variable, sptei, which was initialized as 0 in line 221.
    3. We believe the problem lies in lines 230 and 231, where nights containing data under 60 epochs were skipped, and the sptei was not updated in the next line (i.e., at this point, for these nights, sptei == 0).
    4. It follows that, for nights under 60 epochs, the variable night will have a value of 0.
  4. So, in g.part4.R, when the defaultGuiderOnset variable is set to SPTE_start[j], where “j” is the location index in the list nnights.list (line 265) and that a location index of 0 will result in NULL values, we know the following:
    1. min(sib.cla.sum$night) == 0, for these problematic files
    2. (lines 216-217) first_night = min(sib.cla.sum$night)
      last_night = max(sib.cla.sum$night)
    3. (line 219) nnightlist = first_night:last_night
    4. (line 226) nnights.list = nnightlist
  5. Since “j” will be of value 0 in the first iteration of the for-loop starting at line 265, we will see SPTE_start[j] == NULL, and consequently, defaultGuiderOnset == NULL.
In our specific cases, we can address this issue by running GGIR() separately for input data files that crashed due to this error by skipping their first night in part 4 (by adding the argument "excludefirst.part4 = TRUE" to GGIR()). However, for replicability purposes, it is not ideal that these input files will be run using a slightly different shell script than the rest of the inputs.

We wanted to share these with the rest of the GGIR community in case anyone else has run into a similar issue. If helpful, we would also like to propose a potential fix in the source code so that this won't be an issue for future projects:
  1. In file g.sib.det.R OR g.sib.sum.R, whichever is more convenient and appropriate, consider implementing a change such that the final output is free of rows in which night is equal to 0.
    • Sample code: df <- df %>% filter(night !=0), where df is the name of the output data frame ("metatmp" or "sib.cla.sum," depending on where the change is implemented).
    • The reason why we think this fix might work is because the nights with night = 0 are, by design and reason of too little data, to be skipped. Therefore, dropping those rows should not be a major cause of concern.
We hope some of you might find this information helpful -- thanks!

Best,
Grace
